title: Isaiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 43 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 43.

questions.question: In Isaiah 43, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I will say to the north
questions.explanation: The phrase 'But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob' appears first in the chapter.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He has done for Jacob?
options: He has given Egypt for him
He has called him by name
questions.explanation: The verse states 'for I have redeemed thee' which directly answers the question.

questions.question: What will happen when thou passest through the waters?
options: The flame will kindle upon thee
questions.explanation: The verse states 'When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee'.

questions.question: Who is referred to as the Saviour in Isaiah 43?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'For I am the LORD thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour'.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about those who are precious in His sight?
options: They will be given men for their life
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given men for their life
questions.explanation: The verse states 'I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life'.

questions.question: What does the LORD instruct not to do in Isaiah 43:5?
questions.explanation: The verse begins with 'Fear not: for I am with thee'.

questions.question: From where will the LORD gather His people according to Isaiah 43:5?
options: From the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: The verse states 'I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west'.

questions.question: What will the LORD say to the north?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back'.

questions.question: Who has created everyone called by God's name?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'for I have created him for my glory'.

questions.question: What does the LORD ask to be brought forth in Isaiah 43:8?
options: The blind people that have eyes
questions.correctAnswer: The blind people that have eyes
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Bring forth the blind people that have eyes'.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 43:10, who are the witnesses of the LORD?
options: The servant whom I have chosen
questions.correctAnswer: The servant whom I have chosen
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen'.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD has redeemed Jacob.
questions.explanation: The text states 'for I have redeemed thee'.

questions.question: True or False: The people are to be gathered from the ends of the earth.
questions.explanation: The text states 'bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth'.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will not be with thee when you walk through fire.
questions.explanation: The text states 'when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee', indicating the LORD will be with thee.

questions.question: True or False: The nations are to be gathered together to hear the truth.
questions.explanation: The text states 'let all the nations be gathered together', but it does not say they are to hear the truth.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 43 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who is the savior according to Isaiah 43:11?
options: I, even I, am the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: I, even I, am the LORD
questions.explanation: This is correct because Isaiah 43:11 states, 'I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour.'

questions.question: What does Isaiah 43:12 promise will happen if someone acknowledges the LORD as God?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:12 confirms that 'therefore ye are my witnesses, saith the LORD, that I am God.' Thus, acknowledgment leads to being witnesses.

questions.question: What does the LORD claim about his ability to deliver in Isaiah 43:13?
options: None can deliver out of my hand
questions.correctAnswer: None can deliver out of my hand
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:13 states, 'and there is none that can deliver out of my hand,' indicating the unmatched authority of the LORD.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 43:14 say about the Chaldeans?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 43:14, the LORD says, 'I have brought down all their nobles, and the Chaldeans,' indicating His power over them.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 43:15, who is the creator of Israel?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:15 identifies the LORD as 'your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your King,' encompassing all roles.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 43:16 highlight about the LORD?
options: He makes a way in the sea
questions.correctAnswer: He makes a way in the sea
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:16 states, 'Thus saith the LORD, which maketh a way in the sea,' showcasing His miraculous capabilities.

questions.question: What is promised in Isaiah 43:18 regarding former things?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:18 instructs, 'Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old,' indicating a focus on the new.

questions.question: What new thing does Isaiah 43:19 say the LORD will do?
options: Make a way in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: Make a way in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:19 proclaims, 'I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert,' indicating new provision and guidance.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 43:20, who shall honor the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:20 states, 'The beast of the field shall honour me,' highlighting that all creation acknowledges the LORD.

questions.question: What is the significance of being called by the name of the LORD in Isaiah 43:7?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:7 mentions that those called by His name have been created for His glory, emphasizing their purpose.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 43:3 reveal about the LORD's identity?
options: He is the Holy One of Israel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:3 identifies the LORD as 'the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour,' confirming multiple aspects of His identity.

questions.question: What assurance is given in Isaiah 43:2 concerning trials?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:2 assures, 'when thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee,' providing comfort in trials.

questions.question: Is it true that the LORD claims to have created everyone for His glory in Isaiah 43:7?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:7 states that 'for I have created him for my glory,' confirming that creation is for His glory.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD asks His people to remember the former things according to Isaiah 43:18?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:18 explicitly instructs, 'Remember ye not the former things,' which is a directive against remembering them.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD says He will bring forth the chariot and horse in Isaiah 43:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:17 states, 'Which bringeth forth the chariot and horse,' indicating that He indeed does bring forth the army and power.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 43.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 43:21, why has God formed 'this people'?
options: They shall shew forth my praise
questions.correctAnswer: They shall shew forth my praise
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:21 states explicitly that 'This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 43:22, what is Israel accused of doing instead of calling upon God?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:22 states, 'But thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob; but thou hast been weary of me, O Israel.'

questions.question: What does God claim He has not caused Israel to do in Isaiah 43:23?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:23 says, 'I have not caused thee to serve with an offering, nor wearied thee with incense.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 43:24, what has Israel made God serve with?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:24 states, 'but thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities.'

questions.question: How does God describe His act of forgiveness in Isaiah 43:25?
options: I am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake
I will punish your sins forever
I have no record of your iniquities
questions.correctAnswer: I am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:25 declares, 'I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 43:26, what does God invite Israel to do?
options: Put me in remembrance and plead together
questions.correctAnswer: Put me in remembrance and plead together
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:26 says, 'Put me in remembrance: let us plead together: declare thou, that thou mayest be justified.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chattath' (חַטָּאת) in Isaiah 43:24 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chattath' used in Isaiah 43:24 is commonly translated as 'sin' or 'transgression' in scholarly Hebrew lexicons.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Isaiah 43:18-19 where God says, 'Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old: Behold, I will do a new thing'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:18-19 employs inclusio by framing the passage with a call to forget the former things and a promise of a new work, enclosing the message as a literary bracket.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God as Redeemer and Saviour found in Isaiah 43:1-3?
questions.explanation: John 10:27-30 echoes the theme of God as Redeemer and Saviour, similar to Isaiah 43:1-3 which emphasizes God's protection and calling of His people.

questions.question: Isaiah 43:10 states, 'Ye are my witnesses...'. Which Old Testament passage similarly calls Israel to be God's witnesses?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 42:5 calls Israel to be witnesses of God's promises, paralleling Isaiah 43:10's call for Israel to be God's witnesses.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Isaiah 43:25, where God declares He blotteth out transgressions?
options: Israel has wearied God with their iniquities
God promises to deliver from Babylon
God commands to gather the nations
Jacob is given a new name
questions.correctAnswer: Israel has wearied God with their iniquities
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:24 directly precedes verse 25, describing how Israel has wearied God with their sins and iniquities.

questions.question: The phrase 'I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions' in Isaiah 43:25 is an example of which rhetorical device?
questions.explanation: The phrase uses repetition of 'I, even I' for emphasis, underscoring God's unique role in forgiveness as seen in Isaiah 43:25.

questions.question: Isaiah 43:27 refers to 'Thy first father hath sinned.' Who is traditionally understood to be this 'first father'?
questions.explanation: The 'first father' in Isaiah 43:27 is traditionally interpreted as Adam, the first man who sinned, representing ancestral sin.

questions.question: Isaiah 43:28 states that God has 'profaned the princes of the sanctuary.' What historical context does this reflect?
options: Punishment of corrupt temple leaders during exile
The dedication of the second temple
questions.correctAnswer: Punishment of corrupt temple leaders during exile
questions.explanation: This reflects the historical context of the Babylonian exile when corrupt leaders of the sanctuary were judged, as referenced in Isaiah 43:28.

questions.question: Isaiah 43:21 states 'This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.' True or False: This indicates a special divine purpose for Israel.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:21 clearly assigns a divine purpose to Israel, showing that they were formed to demonstrate God's praise.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 43 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 43:1 teach about God's nature in relation to his people?
options: God is the Creator and Redeemer who claims ownership of His people
God is a distant deity who observes but does not intervene
God's relationship with His people is based on their merit
God only redeems the nation of Israel conditionally
questions.correctAnswer: God is the Creator and Redeemer who claims ownership of His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:1 states, 'the LORD that created thee... Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine,' emphasizing God as Creator and Redeemer who owns His people.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's salvific power is taught in Isaiah 43:2?
options: God protects His people through all trials and dangers
Salvation is based on human strength to overcome adversity
God's protection depends on the people's faithfulness
God's presence is only symbolic, not actual assistance
questions.correctAnswer: God protects His people through all trials and dangers
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:2 assures that 'When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee,' showing God's protective presence in all dangers.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's sovereignty over nations is taught in Isaiah 43:14?
options: God actively uses nations like Babylon to fulfill His redemptive plan
Nations act independently without God's control
God is indifferent to the actions of foreign powers
Babylon acts as an autonomous evil power opposed to God
questions.correctAnswer: God actively uses nations like Babylon to fulfill His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:14 states, 'For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and have brought down all their nobles,' showing God's sovereign use of nations for His purposes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 43:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:11 says, 'I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour,' emphasizing God's unique role as the only Savior.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Isaiah 43:25?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:25 states, 'I... am he that blotteth out thy transgressions,' demonstrating God's merciful forgiveness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 43:19 connect to the broader biblical theme of new creation?
options: It prefigures God's work of making all things new as seen in Revelation
It emphasizes Israel's return from exile without spiritual renewal
It focuses on historical water provisions only
It rejects the idea of God's ongoing creative activity
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures God's work of making all things new as seen in Revelation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:19 says, 'Behold, I will do a new thing,' which aligns with the biblical theme of new creation culminating in Revelation 21.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Isaiah 43:6 make regarding the gathering of God's people?
options: It anticipates the ingathering of the exiles from all nations
It refers only to Israel's initial wilderness wandering
It describes a future physical gathering without spiritual restoration
It signals permanent separation of Israel from other nations
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the ingathering of the exiles from all nations
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:6 says, 'bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth,' anticipating the restoration of Israel from exile.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 43:7 and Isaiah 43:21 teach about God's purpose for His people?
options: God forms His people for His glory and to declare His praise
God's people are self-sufficient and independent of His purpose
God's purpose is limited to national prosperity only
God forms people for judgment rather than praise
questions.correctAnswer: God forms His people for His glory and to declare His praise
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:7 states people are created 'for my glory,' and 43:21 says, 'This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise,' emphasizing God's purpose for His people.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do Isaiah 43:10 and Isaiah 43:12 provide about God's uniqueness and witness?
options: God alone is the true God and Israel is called to be His witness
God shares divine status with other gods and does not require witnesses
God's witness is unnecessary because His existence is self-evident
God acknowledges the legitimacy of foreign gods alongside Himself
questions.correctAnswer: God alone is the true God and Israel is called to be His witness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:10 calls Israel 'my witnesses' and 43:12 states 'I am God,' affirming God's uniqueness and Israel's role as witness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about God's deliverance is taught in Isaiah 43:13 and Isaiah 43:17?
options: God's sovereign power ensures that no one can thwart His saving work
Deliverance depends on human military might and alliances
God's power is limited and can be overcome by enemies
God delivers only occasionally and selectively
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign power ensures that no one can thwart His saving work
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:13 states 'there is none that can deliver out of my hand,' and 43:17 describes enemies as extinguished, highlighting God's sovereign deliverance.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Isaiah 43:8-9 teaches that Israel's God is indistinguishable from other gods because of shared miracles. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God challenges all nations to prove their divine knowledge, showing His unique sovereignty
God admits that many gods share the same powers
The passage suggests that idols can predict the future as well as God
It teaches that God's power is limited to Israel only
questions.correctAnswer: God challenges all nations to prove their divine knowledge, showing His unique sovereignty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:8-9 calls for nations to bring witnesses and declare the truth of God's unique knowledge of former things, asserting His exclusive sovereignty.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and divine forgiveness emerges from Isaiah 43:24-25?
options: Though Israel has burdened God with sin, He promises to forgive for His own sake
Human sin is too great for God to forgive
God demands perfect sacrifices without any sin
Forgiveness is earned by monetary offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Though Israel has burdened God with sin, He promises to forgive for His own sake
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:24 confesses Israel's sinfulness, but 43:25 declares God blots out transgressions for His own sake, showing divine mercy despite human sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Isaiah 43:16?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:16 says, 'which maketh a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters,' demonstrating God's omnipotent power over nature.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 43:22-23 illustrate the theological tension between divine expectation and human response?
options: It shows God's disappointment due to Israel's failure to call upon Him and honor Him properly
It praises Israel's perfect obedience and worship
It claims that God never expected Israel to worship Him
It teaches that sacrifices alone are sufficient for righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's disappointment due to Israel's failure to call upon Him and honor Him properly
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:22-23 reproaches Israel for not calling on God or honoring Him with sacrifices, highlighting human failure against divine expectation.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical role does Isaiah 43:5 fulfill in the biblical narrative?
options: It anticipates God's promise to regather the exiled people from all directions
It describes Israel's initial settlement in Canaan
It predicts the destruction of Israel with no future restoration
It relates to the conquest of Canaan under Joshua only
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates God's promise to regather the exiled people from all directions
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:5 says, 'I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west,' pointing forward to the restoration of Israel after exile.
